verdict: passed — 20/20 new fr values are faithful, idiomatic, glossary- and style-guide-conformant, fit their slots and carry no invisible/bidi characters; 3/3 expected hashes match; one MINOR (F1) records that the tag group 'Type' shares its word with the legacy sort option 'Type' (English keeps Kind/Type distinct), an inherited collision whose remedy sits outside this delta. findings.problem: The English tag-group heading 'Type' is deliberately kept distinct from the Library's sort option, which English calls 'Kind' (en ui.library.sort.kind = 'Kind'; the key's own context note says 'Keep it distinct from the sort option Kind'). In fr both read 'Type': the legacy value ui.library.sort.kind already renders English 'Kind' as 'Type' (fr ui.library.sort.kind = 'Type'), so the toolbar sort option and the rail tag-group header are now the same word for two different concepts on the same Library page.
evidence: fr ui.library.sort.kind = 'Type' (legacy, byte-unchanged by this PR; en counterpart 'Kind')
en/fr ui.library.page.sort = 'Sort' / 'Trier' — the sort option renders under the page toolbar, not in the rail
fr ui.library.filter.tags = 'Étiquettes' — the tag groups sit under that section heading, which is the disambiguating context
findings.why_not_blocker_or_major: The audited value is the faithful and only faithful rendering of English 'Type' for a tag category literally named type ('Catégorie' would misdescribe the group, 'Nature' would invent a taxonomy the wire id does not carry); nothing is misdescribed and no user-facing instruction becomes unsafe. The collision is inherited from the legacy sort label, not introduced by this value, and the 'Étiquettes' section heading keeps the two readable in context.
findings.suggested_wording: Accept 'Type' as-is for this delta. If the wave wants the two distinct, the minimal fix is on the out-of-scope legacy neighbour: ui.library.sort.kind 'Type' -> 'Type de fichier' (under 'Trier'), which then reads 'Trier : Type de fichier' and leaves 'Type' the tag group.

concern_verdicts.a_fidelity: pass — all 12 kind badges name the file kind their English key names; all 7 tag headings name the tag taxonomy group; the generic sentence says 'This file' and names no kind. No omission, addition, negation or polarity error.

The only clash is F1 (Type vs the legacy sort.kind 'Type').
concern_verdicts.c_retained_tokens: pass, judged per token: DOCX, HTML, PDF, PPTX and Markdown retained — each is an acronym/proper format name the fr corpus already writes in Latin (quoted values in per_key_checks). Video is NOT retained ('Vidéo', matching category.video); Code and Audio are identical forms, not retentions of untranslated English. No retention contradicts an existing localized rendering.
concern_verdicts.d_standalone_sentence: pass — 'Ce fichier n’a pas d’aperçu intégré ici.' is grammatical (negation with 'de'), names no kind, carries no placeholder, and parallels ui.library.preview.unsupported ('Un fichier {kind} n’a pas d’aperçu intégré ici.') with the demonstrative the English 'This' calls for.

per_key_checks.assessment: Correct and idiomatic: French uses 'audio' as an invariable noun/adjective for a media type ('fichier audio', 'l’audio'), and the English source itself names the media type while the category group says 'Sounds'. Mirrors the source distinction rather than flattening it.
per_key_checks.retention_judgment: Loanword kept identically to English; French dictionary form, not a retention of an untranslated English word.

per_key_checks.assessment: Same word in French and English; matches the same surface's group label ui.library.category.code = 'Code' with the same spelling. The context note's 'not the filter-rail group' distinction is preserved in meaning (a file kind, not the rail group).

Format acronym retained, as the sidecar allows ('Format names are retained technical tokens'). Consistent with the fr corpus keeping format/product names Latin in prose: 'les fichiers Excel, Word et CSV' (ui.onboarding.tour.attachments.body.3) and 'les PNG, JPG et PDF'.
per_key_checks.retention_judgment: Retained: justified by glossary §1 'technology names … keep their official spelling' + corpus precedent for Word/Excel/PNG/JPG.

per_key_checks.assessment: Retained acronym, and the fr corpus already writes HTML in Latin: 'Aperçu HTML : {title}' (ui.canvas.html_preview.html_preview), 'HTML (.html)' (ui.canvas.create_file_dialog.html_html). No localized rendering exists to contradict.
per_key_checks.retention_judgment: Retained: matches existing fr values, several precedents.

per_key_checks.assessment: Singular of the same surface's group label ui.library.category.images = 'Images'; identical spelling in French. Reads natively as a picture file kind.

Format proper name retained. The fr corpus already does this: 'Copier en Markdown' (ui.chat.transcript_copy.menu.copy_markdown), 'Copié en Markdown', 'Markdown (.md)' (ui.canvas.create_file_dialog.markdown_md), 'visionneuse Markdown' (ui.onboarding.tour.canvas_feature.body.2).
per_key_checks.retention_judgment: Retained: four existing fr values prove it is the settled rendering.

per_key_checks.assessment: Correct singular of the group label ui.library.category.other = 'Autres' and of ui.canvas.files.other = 'Autres'. Kept as a noun/adjective label, not an action. It is not interpolated into the unsupported sentence (that path uses unsupported_generic for the `other` kind), so no agreement trap.
Retained acronym with fr precedent: 'Impossible d’ouvrir ce PDF' (ui.canvas.pdf_preview.this_pdf_could_not_be_opened), 'PDF : {title}', 'les PNG, JPG et PDF'.

Retained format acronym, consistent with DOCX above and with the fr corpus naming PowerPoint formats in Latin ('les fichiers Excel, Word et CSV'). The presentation prose around it stays French ('Ouverture de la présentation', ui.library.preview.pptx_opening).
per_key_checks.retention_judgment: Retained: justified by glossary §1 + corpus precedent.

per_key_checks.assessment: Singular of the same surface's group label ui.library.category.spreadsheets = 'Tableurs' — exactly the same word family, as the brief requires. Note (observation, not a finding): ui.canvas.files.spreadsheets uses 'Feuilles de calcul' on the canvas surface; that cross-surface divergence is pre-existing, outside this PR, and this value correctly follows the Library's own vocabulary.
Correct; and it is the word this namespace already uses for the text tab: ui.library.preview.pptx_text = 'Texte'.
Translated with the accent, matching this surface's group label ui.library.category.video = 'Vidéo' and ui.canvas.files.videos = 'Vidéos'. A retention ('Video') would have contradicted them.

A class label for tags created freely / the empty-category bucket. Masculine singular class label is standard fr UI heading style ('Général', 'Avancé'); no article, no plural, matching the heading's 'a single noun naming the category, not a count'. No existing fr value renders English 'Custom' as a tag category, so there is nothing to contradict.
Same word in French, and identical to the sibling ui.library.sort.kind family vocabulary; correct for a group of format tags ('pdf', 'csv'). Distinguished from tag_category.type as English is.
Glossary §2 binds project -> 'projet' for fr ('project | translate | projet'); honoured. Same spelling as the glossary's citation form, correctly capitalised as a heading.

Identical to the fr rendering of the neighbouring filter section (ui.library.filter.source = 'Source'), which is the same English word; the context note's distinction (tag group vs filter section) is a role distinction, not a wording one, and English makes the same choice.
Exactly the value the same namespace already uses for the Status filter section: ui.library.filter.status = 'Statut'. Consistent register and term.

The settled fr word for a topic/subject ('Sujet' — e.g. ui.teamBridge.create.topic = 'Sujet (facultatif)'). Not 'Thème', which this corpus reserves for appearance themes (ui.chat.pickers.theme.title = 'Thème'). Correct choice; the rail places it first, as the note says.
per_key_checks.retention_judgment: Translated; 'Thème' would have collided with the appearance-theme vocabulary.

per_key_checks.assessment: The faithful rendering of English 'Type' for a tag category literally named type, and it keeps the fr corpus's one word for this concept (every 'Kind'/'type' surface in fr reads 'Type'). The one caveat is F1: the same word already labels the sort-by-kind option, because the legacy ui.library.sort.kind renders English 'Kind' as 'Type'.

per_key_checks.source: This file has no in-app preview here.
per_key_checks.current_text: Ce fichier n’a pas d’aperçu intégré ici.
per_key_checks.assessment: Grammatical and native; names no kind. It parallels the templated sibling exactly — fr ui.library.preview.unsupported = 'Un fichier {kind} n’a pas d’aperçu intégré ici.' — swapping the indefinite 'Un fichier {kind}' for the demonstrative 'Ce fichier', which is the right move for 'This file'. Negation takes 'de' correctly ('n’a pas d’aperçu'), no placeholder, no trailing punctuation, U+2019 apostrophes as the style guide requires, 40 chars vs 37 English (+8%, well inside the guide's 15-25% growth). Rendered only for the `other` kind (library-viewers.tsx:107-110), so it must not name one — it does not.
